claims.text: The material under consideration is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix.
Surface nanostructuring produces a nanostructured surface on the coating.
Surface nanostructuring enhances the surface roughness of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Surface nanostructuring enhances the hardness of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The enhanced roughness and hardness caused by nanostructuring improve wear resistance.
A surface-nanostructured FeNiCrCoCu coating will have better wear resistance than an unchanged coating tested under identical conditions.
The predicted improvement applies from -20°C to 100°C.
The predicted improvement applies at sliding velocities from 0.1 m/s to 10 m/s.
The predicted improvement applies at wear depths up to 100 μm.
Variations in nanostructure morphology and distribution may alter the predicted wear response.
Nanoindentation and SEM analysis of worn surfaces can resolve microscopic deformation during wear.

contradictions.description: The proposed SEM and nanoindentation measurements are described as analyses of worn surfaces, which are post-wear measurements, while the experiment is claimed to resolve microscopic deformation during wear. No in situ method is specified.
